candidate_relations.reason: Sarcoidosis could cause uveitis and lymphadenopathy but is a granulomatous inflammatory condition, not a lymphomatous malignancy. The clinical picture with hemorrhagic hypopyon, bilateral lymphadenopathy, and acellular proteinaceous AC tap strongly favors lymphoma over sarcoidosis. This is an incompatible etiology.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Sarcoidosis is a specific etiology of uveitis incompatible with lymphoma as the cause

candidate_relations.label: Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma
candidate_relations.reason: The extensive bilateral peripheral lymphadenopathy (preauricular, submandibular, cervical, supraclavicular, axillary) is characteristic of systemic lymphoma such as mantle cell lymphoma, not PCNSL which by definition lacks systemic nodal involvement. PCNSL is an incompatible subtype/scope.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: PCNSL is a distinct lymphoma subtype (typically DLBCL) confined to CNS/eye without systemic nodal involvement; mantle cell lymphoma is a systemic B-cell lymphoma with nodal disease

candidate_relations.label: Intraocular lymphoma
candidate_relations.reason: Intraocular lymphoma correctly identifies the lymphomatous nature of the ocular disease and is compatible with the reference diagnosis, but it is a broader/parent category that does not specify mantle cell lymphoma as the subtype. The reference requires the specific systemic diagnosis of mantle cell lymphoma.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Intraocular lymphoma is the ocular manifestation/component of the systemic mantle cell lymphoma; it lacks the specific systemic subtype designation

case_quality_flags: Anterior chamber paracentesis yielded acellular proteinaceous material, limiting cytologic confirmation; diagnosis inferred from systemic lymphadenopathy pattern and clinical presentation
Mantle cell lymphoma with ocular involvement is rare; the specific subtype would typically require lymph node biopsy with immunohistochemistry/flow cytometry not described in the record
